claim: Raft must maintain safety under all non-Byzantine conditions, including network delays, partitions, and packet loss, duplication and reordering.
quote: They ensure safety (never returning an incorrect result) under all non-Byzantine conditions, including network delays, partitions, and packet loss, duplication, and reordering.

claim: Raft's formal specification models the network as able to reorder, drop, and duplicate messages.
quote: The network may reorder, drop, and duplicate messages.

locator: Section 2 'Replicated state machines', p.2, properties list, second bullet
claim: Raft assumes crash-recovery faults: a server fails by stopping, and may later recover its state from stable storage and rejoin the cluster.
quote: Servers are assumed to fail by stopping; they may later recover from state on stable storage and rejoin the cluster.

locator: Section 11.1 'Overview of consensus algorithms', opening paragraph
claim: Raft handles fail-stop but not Byzantine failures, so servers are assumed not to behave arbitrarily (no lying or collusion); it also does not rely on time for safety.
quote: Like Raft, these algorithms handle fail-stop but not Byzantine failures, and they do not rely on time for safety (the key properties of practical consensus algorithms can be found in Section 2.1).

locator: Section 2 'Replicated state machines', p.2, properties list, third bullet
claim: Raft does not depend on timing to keep the logs consistent: faulty clocks and extreme message delays can, at worst, cause availability problems, not incorrect results, so no synchronized clocks are required.
quote: They do not depend on timing to ensure the consistency of the logs: faulty clocks and extreme message delays can, at worst, cause availability problems.

locator: README.md, 'Features', bullet 'More efficient lease-based linearizable read-only queries', sub-bullet 3
claim: The core library does not depend on clocks, but its optional lease-based linearizable read optimization does rely on the clocks of all machines in the Raft group.
quote: this approach relies on the clock of the all the machines in raft group

claim: Raft retries failed RPCs indefinitely, so when a crashed follower or candidate restarts the pending RPC completes and it rejoins the cluster.
quote: Raft handles these failures by retrying indefinitely; if the crashed server restarts, then the RPC will complete successfully.

claim: Raft servers persist enough information to stable storage to survive a restart safely, which is why persistent state must outlive a crash.
quote: Raft servers must persist enough information to stable storage to survive server restarts safely.

locator: README.md, 'Usage', 'After creating a Node' responsibilities, step 2
claim: The etcd raft library requires that no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk and all entries from earlier Ready batches have been written, making reboot-and-rejoin a designed-for event.
quote: It is important that no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk, and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while entries from the same batch are being persisted).

locator: README.md, 'Usage', 'After creating a Node' responsibilities, step 1
claim: On each Ready the library directs the application to write Entries, then HardState and Snapshot, to persistent storage in that order.
quote: Write Entries, HardState and Snapshot to persistent storage in order, i.e. Entries first, then HardState and Snapshot if they are not empty.
